metaData.originalTitle: 小红书引擎架构团队 ICDE 2026 新成果：CCD 感知编排突破多核 CPU 向量搜索性能天花板
metaData.title: Xiaohongshu Engine Architecture Team's ICDE 2026 Breakthrough: CCD-Aware Orchestration Breaks Multi-Core CPU Vector Search Performance Ceiling
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: The Xiaohongshu Engine Architecture team published a paper at ICDE 2026, proposing a load-aware and thread orchestration framework for multi-core CPU CCD architectures. By leveraging hot-cold adaptive mapping and topology-aware task stealing, it boosts vector search throughput by up to 3.7x and reduces P999 tail latency by 90%.
metaData.summary: This article details the latest research results from the Xiaohongshu Engine Architecture team, presented at ICDE 2026. The team systematically analyzed the core performance bottlenecks of industrial-grade vector ANNS services on AMD EPYC multi-Chiplet (CCD) architecture CPUs, including cross-CCD cache invalidation, cache pollution caused by Hot-Hot co-location, and the destruction of cache affinity due to global task stealing. To address these issues, the team proposed a CCD-aware adaptive thread orchestration framework. The framework comprises three core modules: a unified task submission interface compatible with HNSW and IVF algorithms; a hot-cold aware mapping scheduler that uses a greedy double-ended scanning algorithm to pair hot and cold tables on the same CCD, achieving traffic balance and avoiding cache contention; and a topology-aware hierarchical task stealing mechanism that uses three levels of stealing priority (local, same CCD, cross-CCD) to reduce the cross-CCD task stealing rate from 80% to below 5% while ensuring load balance. Experimental results on Xiaohongshu's real-world workloads show that on a 96-core CPU, the framework achieves up to a 3.7x throughput improvement, a 60%-90% reduction in P999 tail latency, a 6%-30% reduction in L3 cache miss rate, and a 20%-80% reduction in CPU stall time. This work provides a systematic solution for optimizing the performance of industrial-grade vector retrieval on new CPU architectures.

mainPoints.point: Under multi-core CCD architectures, existing thread scheduling frameworks, due to their topology-agnostic nature, cause severe cross-CCD cache invalidation and performance bottlenecks.
mainPoints.explanation: CPUs like the AMD EPYC feature a CCD architecture with independent L3 caches. However, existing schedulers (e.g., OpenMP, bthread) do not account for this topology, causing vector data to be repeatedly loaded across multiple CCDs. This leads to high cache miss rates, significant CPU stalls waiting for memory data, and actual throughput far below theoretical linear scaling.

mainPoints.point: The hot-cold adaptive mapping algorithm effectively solves the cache pollution problem caused by the co-location of multiple hot tables through Hot-Cold pairing.
mainPoints.explanation: Based on online traffic estimation, the scheduler pairs high-traffic hot tables with low-traffic cold tables on the same CCD. This prevents multiple hot tables from competing for limited L3 cache space and evicting each other. A sliding window mechanism adapts to dynamic changes in business load, ensuring balanced traffic across all CCDs.

mainPoints.point: The topology-aware hierarchical task stealing strategy minimizes cross-CCD task migration while ensuring load balance.
mainPoints.explanation: The framework establishes three levels of stealing priority: local queues first, then stealing within the same CCD, and finally strictly limiting cross-CCD stealing. This strategy drastically reduces the cross-CCD task stealing rate from 75%-80% to 5%-10%, resolving the long-standing engineering conflict between cache affinity and load balancing.

keyQuotes: Existing thread scheduling frameworks are completely unaware of the topological characteristics of the CCD architecture, leading to massive cross-CCD cache invalidation. This means that increased computing resources not only fail to translate into performance gains but also exacerbate system performance degradation due to cache pollution and memory bandwidth contention.

By using a hot-cold pairing strategy to avoid Hot-Hot co-location, traffic balance across all CCDs is achieved. A sliding window mechanism ensures smooth transitions and adapts to dynamic changes in business load.

By being aware of the CPU's physical topology and establishing three levels of stealing priority, cross-CCD task migration is minimized while load balance is ensured, resolving the long-standing engineering conflict between cache affinity and load balancing.
Without replacing hardware or modifying the core index code, we achieved up to a 3.7x throughput improvement and up to a 90% reduction in tail latency.

relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Xiaohongshu's Quality and Efficiency R&D team shared their self-developed GUI Agent intelligent testing system at QCon Beijing 2026.
